Flag occurrence records

Source: R/flag.R
flag_occurrences.Rd

Runs a set of record tests over species occurrence records and writes one flag per record per test. Nothing is removed and no threshold is baked in: a cleaning rule is a set of tests, applied afterwards with has_flag() or summarised with tally_flags().

Usage

flag_occurrences(
  x,
  tests = NULL,
  columns = occ_columns(),
  reference = c("OccurrenceCleaner", "CoordinateCleaner"),
  gazetteers = NULL,
  land_scale = 110,
  buffers = NULL,
  settings = NULL,
  duplicate_by = NULL,
  duplicate_cell = NULL,
  out = NULL,
  keep = NULL,
  part_rows = 2e+06,
  resume = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A data frame, a vectra_node, or a path (file or directory).

tests

Character vector of test names, see flag_tests(). Default default_tests(). A test whose fields are missing from x is an error.

columns

Field names, see occ_columns().

reference

"OccurrenceCleaner" (own gazetteers, the default) or "CoordinateCleaner" (that package's tables, read at run time). See reference_info().

gazetteers

Named list of user-supplied reference layers, each replacing the reference layer of one test. Point tests (capital, centroid, institution, gbif_headquarters) take a data frame with longitude and latitude columns (named lon/lat, longitude/latitude or decimalLongitude/decimalLatitude, any case). Polygon tests (sea, urban, country_mismatch) take an sf or sfc object of POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON geometries in longitude and latitude; for sea they are the land, and for country_mismatch the features need at least one code column (iso_a2, iso_a3, adm0_a3 or code, any case). Each layer is indexed once per call, and its size and MD5 checksum are recorded in the reference label of the output. range takes species range polygons (see test_range), sampling a table of records per country for the sampling correction of test_outlier, and habitat a table of genus habitats for test_habitat (see reference_habitat()). The land layer given for sea is also the land of the habitat tests.

land_scale

Natural Earth scale of the land layer for sea and the habitat tests: 110 (the default of CoordinateCleaner's cc_sea(); its clean_coordinates() uses seas_scale = 50), 50, or 10 (downloaded on first use, see download_reference()).

buffers

Named list overriding buffer distances in metres for capital (10000), centroid (1000), institution (100), gbif_headquarters (1000), range (0), aohi (10000), sea_nonmarine (0) and land_marine (0), or in degrees for zero (0.5). Unnamed entries keep the defaults.

settings

Named list overriding the options of the grouped tests, one entry per test, each a named list; unnamed options keep their defaults, which are CoordinateCleaner's. See test_outlier, test_age_outlier, test_spatiotemporal_outlier, test_age_range_outlier, test_dataset_ddmm and test_dataset_rounded.

duplicate_by

Additional column names a duplicate must share (as CoordinateCleaner's additions), for example an event date.

duplicate_cell

Cell size in degrees. When given, coordinates are binned to this grid before comparing duplicates, so "same cell and species" counts.

out

Output directory for streamed input (required then, ignored for a data frame).

keep

Column names copied next to the flags in streamed output, for grouping in tally_flags() (taxon, year, uncertainty, ...). The id column of columns is kept when present.

part_rows

Target rows per output part file for streamed input: a part is written once at least this many rows have accumulated, and at the end of each input unit.

resume

Skip input units whose output already exists.

verbose

Report progress for streamed input.

Value

For a data frame: x with an integer column flags and one logical column flag_<test> per test, class occ_flags added in front, and attributes occ_tests, occ_layout_version, occ_reference and occ_columns. summary() reports the share of records each test flags, plot() draws it or maps the records. For streamed input: an object of class occ_flagged describing the output directory, which tally_flags() accepts; the parts are .vtr files holding the id and keep columns and flags, readable with vectra::tbl().

Details

The grouped tests (outlier, the three fossil outlier tests and the two dataset tests) compare a record with the other records of its species, taxon or dataset; they run in a pass over the whole input before the record tests, which on streamed input reads every file once or twice more.

The input is either a data frame, or an on-disk table streamed in chunks: a vectra_node (from vectra::tbl_parquet(), vectra::tbl_csv(), vectra::tbl()), a path to a Parquet file or directory of Parquet parts (such as a GBIF snapshot), or a path to a .vtr or delimited text file. For a directory each file is one resumable unit of work; the return follows the input, see Value.

Tests

See flag_tests() for the layout. Tests equivalent to CoordinateCleaner use its default buffers: capital 10 km, centroid 1 km, institution 100 m, gbif_headquarters 1 km, zero 0.5 degrees. Proximity tests are closed balls in WGS84 geodesic distance. Records failing invalid are given no spatial flag.

Documented differences to CoordinateCleaner 3.0.1, each verified in the package tests:

  • CoordinateCleaner approximates each buffer circle by an inscribed polygon (72 vertices for capital, centroid, gbif_headquarters; 40 for institution), so a record between 99.9 % (capital, centroid, gbif_headquarters) or 99.7 % (institution) of the buffer and the buffer itself is flagged here and may not be there. Everything CoordinateCleaner flags is flagged here.

  • cc_zero's 0.5 degree buffer is interpreted by terra as 0.5 metres, so CoordinateCleaner 3.0.1 flags only exact zeros; this package applies the documented 0.5 degree radius.

  • country_mismatch compares the record's code with the ISO alpha-2 code, the ISO alpha-3 code and the Natural Earth ADM0_A3 code of the country polygon the point falls in, taking the ISO codes from Natural Earth's ISO_A2_EH and ISO_A3_EH columns, which are filled where ISO_A2 and ISO_A3 hold -99 (France, Norway, Kosovo); CoordinateCleaner compares ISO_A3 only, so it flags every record in France and Norway. Records without a code, or at sea, are flagged as in CoordinateCleaner.

  • duplicate on streamed input is evaluated within each input file (Parquet part), not across the whole table.

  • outlier flags the records of outlier cells in the raster approximation (species of 10,000 records or more, or thinning = TRUE); in CoordinateCleaner 3.0.1 that path never flags a record.

  • age_outlier and spatiotemporal_outlier draw ages from a stream seeded per taxon, so they agree with cf_age() and cf_outl() in distribution; when every age range has zero width the flags are identical.

  • dataset_rounded leaves datasets below min_unique_ds_size untested, where cd_round() stops with an error; the dataset tests do not flag records without a dataset key.

  • With the default reference the gazetteers are rebuilt from the original sources; reference = "CoordinateCleaner" uses that package's own tables, and gazetteers replaces the layer of single tests, as the ref arguments of CoordinateCleaner's functions do.

Examples

x <- data.frame(species = c("a", "a", "b", "c"),
                decimalLongitude = c(12.58, 0, 16.37, 2.35),
                decimalLatitude = c(55.67, 0, 48.21, 48.85))
f <- flag_occurrences(x, tests = c("invalid", "zero", "gbif_headquarters", "capital"))
f[, c("species", "flags", "flag_zero", "flag_gbif_headquarters", "flag_capital")]
